title: The alphabet and spelling your name
goal: Say the French letters and accents, spell your name aloud, and ask how a word is spelled.

items.note: Both word orders are correct and very common.
On a form, Nom means your family name.

drills.prompt: Which letter is called “ji” in French?
drills.explain: J = ji, G = gé. They are the reverse of English, so they are easy to mix up.

drills.prompt: How does the French letter E sound?
drills.explain: French E is a short “uh”. The “ee” sound is the letter I.

drills.prompt: How do you spell the “ss” in the name Rousseau aloud?
drills.explain: Say the number first: deux S (or double S).

blocks.body: Listen to the letters. Some sound like English, but **E, G, I, J, U, R** are very different.

blocks.title: The same 26 letters, different names
blocks.body:
French uses the same alphabet as English, but the **names** of the letters change. When you spell your name at a bank, a clinic or on the phone, people will use these names.

The written names below (like [[bé]] or [[ji]]) are only there to show the sound. Tap the speaker to hear each one.

blocks.note: *Tricky* = the letters English speakers mix up most. **G and J are swapped** compared with English. Watch the vowels too: French **I** sounds like English **E** (“ee”), and French **E** is “uh”.

blocks.note: When you spell, say **the letter first, then the accent**: [[e accent aigu]], not “accent aigu e”. You will also meet â, û and ï (as in the name Anaïs).

blocks.title: Asking and answering
blocks.pattern: Ça s'écrit comment ? / Comment ça s'écrit ? → letter, letter, letter…
blocks.note: Both questions mean “How is it spelled?”. To answer, you can start with [[Mon nom, c'est…]] (my last name is…) or [[Mon prénom, c'est…]] (my first name is…). For two identical letters, say [[deux L]], [[deux S]]. For a hyphen, say [[trait d'union]].

examples.fr: Mon prénom, c'est Raj : R, A, J.
examples.en: My first name is Raj: R, A, J.

examples.fr: Mon nom, c'est Rousseau : R, O, U, deux S, E, A, U.
examples.en: My last name is Rousseau: R, O, U, double S, E, A, U.

examples.fr: Hélène : H, E accent aigu, L, E accent grave, N, E.
examples.en: Hélène: H, E acute, L, E grave, N, E.

blocks.body:
- **E vs I:** French [[e]] is a short “uh”; French [[i]] is “ee”. An English speaker who says “ee” for E will be heard as saying I.
- **G vs J:** [[gé]] rhymes with *say*, [[ji]] rhymes with *see*. Memory trick: listen to the vowel at the end: G ends in **é**, J ends in **i**.
- **U:** say “ee”, keep your tongue there, then round your lips as if to whistle. That is French [[u]]. (More in lesson 3.)
- **R:** [[erre]] uses the throat r, like a soft gargle.
- **Y** is [[i grec]], literally “Greek i”, and **W** is [[double vé]], literally “double V”.

- **Accents are not decoration.** They can change the word: [[a]] (has) and [[à]] (to, at); [[ou]] (or) and [[où]] (where). Always write them.
- **Capital letters keep their accents** in careful writing: [[ÉCOLE]], [[HÉLÈNE]]. Both the Office québécois de la langue française and the Académie française recommend this.
- **ç only goes before a, o, u**, to make an *s* sound: [[ça]], [[français]], [[François]]. Never before e or i (c already sounds like s there).
- **Order:** spell [[E accent aigu]], not “accent aigu E”.

- You will also hear [[Ça s'épelle comment ?]] (*épeler* = to spell), in Québec as in France. It means the same as [[Ça s'écrit comment ?]].
- **Hyphenated first names** are very common: [[Marie-Ève]], [[Jean-François]], [[Anne-Marie]]. Say [[trait d'union]] for the hyphen when you spell.
- On Canadian and Québec forms, **[[Nom]] means your family name** and **[[Prénom]] your first name**. Fill in [[Nom]] with your *last* name.
- In Québec, married people legally keep their birth name, so [[madame Côté]] may be married to [[monsieur Tremblay]].
- On the phone, people make letters clear with a word: [[M comme Montréal]] (M as in Montréal), [[B comme Bernard]].

examples.fr: Marie-Ève : M, A, R, I, E, trait d'union, E accent grave, V, E.
examples.en: Marie-Ève: M, A, R, I, E, hyphen, E grave, V, E.

accept: Quel est votre prénom, s'il vous plaît ?
blocks.explain: prénom = first name; nom = last name. Polite: s'il vous plaît.
Before o, a plain c sounds like k. The cédille (ç) makes it an s sound.

blocks.prompt: A last name is spelled aloud. Type the name.
accept: R O U S S E A U

blocks.explain: Ça s'écrit comment ? and Comment ça s'écrit ? are both correct.

models.en: Hello! My last name is Côté: C, O circumflex, T, E acute. My first name is Marie-Ève: M, A, R, I, E, hyphen, E grave, V, E.

summary:
- Say the 26 letters, especially the tricky **E, I, G, J, U, R**
- Name the accents: [[accent aigu, accent grave, accent circonflexe, cédille, tréma]]
- Spell your name with [[deux L]] or [[trait d'union]] when needed
- Ask [[Ça s'écrit comment ?]] and understand [[nom]] (last name) and [[prénom]] (first name)
